title: 1911 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship
text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1911 | image = | dates = | teams = | connacht = Galway | munster = Limerick | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = Antrim | matches = | poty = | team = Kilkenny | titles = 5th | captain = [[Sim Walton]] | manager = | team2 = Tipperary | captain2 = | manager2 = | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1910|1910]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1912|1912]] }} The '''All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1911''' was the 25th series of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], [[Ireland]]'s premier [[hurling]] [[single-elimination tournament|knock-out competition]]. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the championship, beating [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] 3–3 to 2–1 in a substitute [[1911 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=28 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }} ==Format== '''All-Ireland Championship''' ''Semi-finals:'' (2 matches) The four provincial representatives made up the semi-final pairings. Two teams are eliminated at this stage while the two winning teams advance to the All-Ireland final. ''Final:'' (1 match) The winners of the two semi-finals contest this game with the winners being declared All-Ireland champions. ==Results== ===[[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{football box | date =8 October 1911

Final | team1 = {{GG|Kilkenny|hurling}} | score = 4–6 – 3–1 | team2 = {{GG|Dublin|hurling}} | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium =[[Portlaoise]] }} ===[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{football box | date = Final | team1 = {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} | score = 5–3 – 4–3 | team2 = {{GG|Tipperary|hurling}} | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium = }} ===[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{football box | date = 26 November 1911

Final | team1 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] | score = Cancelled | team2 = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium = [[Cork Athletic Grounds]], [[Cork (city)|Cork]]| }} ---- {{football box | date = 12 May 1912
Refixed Final | team1 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] | score = Cancelled | team2 = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium = [[Cork Athletic Grounds]], [[Cork (city)|Cork]] | }} ---- {{football box | date = 28 July 1912
Substitute Final | team1 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] | score = 3–3 – 2–1 | team2 = [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] | goals1 = | goals2 = | stadium = [[Fraher Field]], [[Dungarvan]]| }} ==Championship statistics== ===Results=== * The All-Ireland final between [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] is never played. The original fixture was cancelled due to the state of the pitch at the [[Cork Athletic Grounds]]. The final was postponed until the 12 May, however, Limerick refused to play in that game. A substitute contest took place at [[Fraher Field]] on 28 July. The [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]] nominated [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] to play Kilkenny, with the latter winning the game by 3-3 to 2-1. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==Sources== * Corry, Eoghan, ''The GAA Book of Lists'' (Hodder Headline Ireland, 2005). * Donegan, Des, ''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' (DBA Publications Limited, 2005). ==See also== {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships|1911]] [[Category:1911 in hurling|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] [[Category:1911 in Irish sport]]
